findings.title: Imported HTML is stored and rendered unsanitized
findings.body: TopicEmbed.import appends the source URL into the post body with raw string interpolation (`<a href='#{url}'>`) and saves the whole document via PostCreator with cook_method raw_html and skip_validations. Post#cook then returns raw unchanged whenever cook_method is raw_html, so the normal PrettyText/Sanitize pipeline never runs. Cooked HTML is rendered with `raw` in the embed view and on the topic page. RSS items (PollFeed also runs CGI.unescapeHTML on the body, turning escaped markup back into tags) and any page fetched for an embed can therefore plant script, event handlers, or a quote-breaking URL such as http://host/?q='><script>… and get stored XSS in the forum origin. The existing sanitize gem is not used, and the topic embed spec locks in cooked == raw.

findings.title: Embed template has invalid ERB (`end if`)
findings.body: The header conditional is closed with `<%- end if %>`, which is not valid Ruby inside ERB. Rendering the success path (a topic id was found and best.html.erb is rendered) raises a SyntaxError/Template::Error, so the embed iframe 500s whenever a discussion already exists. It must be `<% end %>`.

findings.title: Feed poll crashes on typical RSS items
findings.body: poll_feed always does `CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` and then TopicEmbed.import. SimpleRSS leaves `content` nil for ordinary RSS 2.0 items that only have `description`/`summary`, so the first such item raises NoMethodError and the hourly job stops, importing nothing after it. String#scrub also does not exist on Ruby 2.0/1.9, which this app still references. There is no per-item rescue, and title/link can be missing the same way. Use a fallback (`content` or `description` or empty string), guard nil, and isolate item failures.

findings.title: import_remote uses Kernel#open on attacker-influenced URLs
findings.body: import_remote calls `open(url).read` without `require 'open-uri'` (unlike PollFeed) and without an http(s)-only client, timeout, or redirect check. If open-uri has not been loaded, Kernel#open treats the URL as a local filename and the fetch fails (Disqus import and embed retrieval blow up). Once open-uri is loaded, it follows redirects to any host with no read timeout, and non-URI strings fall through to file open or pipe execution. Embed URLs are supplied by visitors (TopicRetriever only compares URI#host to embeddable_host, not the scheme, and does not re-check redirects), and PollFeed does the same `open` on feed_polling_url. That is SSRF against internal HTTP services, worker hangs, and, for a non-http setting or feed link, local file read.

findings.title: postMessage origin check is a substring match
findings.body: The resize listener accepts a message when `discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) !== -1`. That is the wrong direction and is not an origin equality check. Any origin that is a prefix/substring of the configured forum URL passes, for example origin `http://forum.example.co` against discourseUrl `http://forum.example.com`, or any shorter prefix. A page that can postMessage to the host page (opener or another frame) can then set the embed iframe height. Compare the message origin to the parsed origin of discourseUrl (scheme, host, and port) instead.

findings.title: Embed controller specs assert the wrong control flow
findings.body: The success example expects `TopicRetriever.new` and `retrieve` to run inside the request. EmbedController#best does not do that; it calls `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, …)` and renders loading. That expectation fails. The other success example renders best.html.erb, which currently cannot compile (`end if`), so the after-hook `response.should be_success` fails as well. The specs will not catch the enqueue/host/throttle behavior that actually shipped.

findings.title: Cache miss runs a full feed import and drops HTTP fallback
findings.body: When feed polling is enabled, perform_retrieve synchronously runs `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` (download and import every feed item) inside the per-URL retrieve job, then only calls fetch_http if that returns normally and the URL is still missing. Any exception from the feed (network error, nil content, bad item) aborts the job before the single-page HTTP fetch, so the embed stays on the loading page forever. A single comment embed also triggers a full import with no timeout isolation.

findings.title: Unauthenticated embed GETs enqueue unbounded jobs
findings.body: best only checks that the Referer host equals embeddable_host, then enqueues retrieve_topic for whatever embed_url was passed. Referer is trivial to spoof, embed_url is not checked against embeddable_host or a rate limit in the request, and the Redis throttle lives inside the job and is per URL. An anonymous client can fill the Sidekiq queue with unique URLs; each job still does work (host parse, Redis, sometimes HTTP). Validate the embed URL host before enqueue and throttle enqueues.

findings.title: embed_url is varchar(255) with a unique index
findings.body: embed_url is a Rails string column (varchar 255) and is uniquely indexed. Article and tracking URLs routinely exceed 255 characters. Insert then raises on PostgreSQL, TopicEmbed.create! rolls the import back, and that URL can never be embedded. Store embed_url as text (and keep the unique index).

findings.title: Disqus import now depends on a live remote fetch and drops category
findings.body: The importer used to create a local topic from the export (permalink stub, optional -c category) and then attach comments. It now calls TopicEmbed.import_remote, which GETs t[:link] and returns nothing usable if the historical URL 404s, redirects oddly, or open() raises. The exception is not rescued inside the thread loop, so one dead link aborts the rest of the file (the ensure only restores the email blacklist and rate limiter). The category option and category_id lookup were removed, and TopicEmbed.import has no category argument, so surviving imports also land in the wrong category.

findings.title: Post jobs are enqueued inside the outer import transaction
findings.body: import wraps PostCreator.create in Topic.transaction. PostCreator commits its own nested transaction by joining that outer one, then enqueue_jobs (process_post, feature_topic_users) runs before Topic.transaction commits. If TopicEmbed.create! then fails (unique embed_url race, null id), the outer transaction rolls the post back but the jobs are already queued and run against a missing row. Even on success they can run before commit. Enqueue only after the outer transaction commits, and rescue RecordNotUnique so a raced import reuses the existing embed instead of erroring.

findings.title: Throttle key can stick forever if expire is skipped
findings.body: retrieved_recently? uses SETNX and then a separate EXPIRE of 60 seconds. If the process dies between those calls, the key remains with no TTL and that embed URL is never fetched again for non-staff users (they stay on the loading page). Use a single SET key 1 NX EX 60 so the lock cannot outlive the throttle window.
